messages.text: Mercedes set to run ADUO engine upgrade in Las Vegas with one driver

metadata.summary: World champions Mercedes will bring their ADUO turbocharger upgrade to this weekend's Las Vegas Grand Prix, although George Russell will not use it to avoid having to take another grid penalty in his bid for second place in the Drivers' Championship.
metadata.content: Mercedes confirm ADUO turbo upgrade ready for Las Vegas GP with Kimi Antonelli set to run new engine part | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Mercedes confirm ADUO turbo upgrade ready for Las Vegas GP with Kimi Antonelli set to run new engine part Silver Arrows expecting to run ADUO update on Kimi Antonelli's car only as use of another turbo for George Russell would trigger fresh grid drop; watch the Las Vegas GP this weekend on Sky Sports F1, with qualifying at 4am on Saturday and the race at 4am on Sunday Tuesday 17 November 2026 15:59, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Following Mercedes claiming the 2026 F1 Constructors' Championship, team principal Toto Wolff sends a message to the team's workforce back at base World champions Mercedes will bring their ADUO turbocharger upgrade to this weekend's Las Vegas Grand Prix, although George Russell will not use it to avoid having to take another grid penalty in his bid for second place in the Drivers' Championship. Mercedes in June were granted one chance to upgrade their power unit this season after being found to be between two and four per cent behind the best-performing internal combustion engine - which was unexpectedly judged to be Red Bull's - by the FIA in the year's first ADUO (Additional Development and Upgrade Opportunities) assessment window. messages.text: Rooney contemplated suicide at ‘lowest point’ of Man Utd career

metadata.summary: Wayne Rooney has revealed there was a period in his Manchester United career where he contemplated suicide.
metadata.content: Wayne Rooney says he contemplated suicide during ‘lowest point’ of Manchester United career | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Wayne Rooney says he contemplated suicide during ‘lowest point’ of Manchester United career Wayne Rooney has revealed he considered taking his own life while playing for Manchester United; this article discusses mental health and suicide, which some readers may find distressing; if you have been affected by this story, support and guidance are available at sky.com/viewersupport Tuesday 17 November 2026 15:25, UK Image: Wayne Rooney has spoken candidly about his mental health struggles Wayne Rooney has revealed there was a period in his Manchester United career where he contemplated suicide. The former England striker revealed that, despite enjoying success on the pitch, he was struggling with his mental health off it. Newly married and a father to eldest son Kai, Rooney would sometimes spend two days drinking at home. Speaking on the Life at the Midpoint with Gabby Logan podcast, he admitted that, at his lowest point, he had contemplated taking his own life. "I can look back and say I was selfish, but I knew I was going through something which I was really struggling to deal with. Then I didn't want Kai seeing me like that, so that's why I'd hide away as well," Rooney said. "I got to a place where you're contemplating suicide. You just didn't want to be around anyone. messages.text: Mowbray steps down from Blackburn due to health issues

metadata.summary: Tony Mowbray has stepped down from his role as Blackburn Rovers head coach due to health issues.
metadata.content: Tony Mowbray steps down as Blackburn Rovers head coach due to health issues | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Tony Mowbray steps down as Blackburn Rovers head coach due to health issues Tuesday 17 November 2026 11:14, UK Image: Tony Mowbray has left Blackburn Tony Mowbray has stepped down from his role as Blackburn Rovers head coach due to health issues. The 62-year-old returned to football at West Brom last year following his recovery from bowel cancer, before taking charge at Blackburn in June. In a statement, Mowbray said: "Unfortunately, due to health issues, I have to step back from my role as head coach of Blackburn Rovers. "I'm immensely proud of this group of players. Their dedication and professionalism have given us some memorable performances and wins, and I've loved working with them. "Thank you to my coaching staff for all your hard work and for the support you've given me. It's been a pleasure working alongside you. "To the fans, thank you for the way you've supported me and the team this season. I've always tried to give you a team that you can be proud of. Your support has meant a great deal to me. "I'm grateful to the owners and Suhail [Shaikh, Blackburn's chief operating officer] for giving me the opportunity to lead this great club once again. "I'd ask that you give me and my family privacy at this time. "Thank you for your understanding. Tony." Mowbray had enjoyed an impressive start to his second spell at Blackburn. messages.text: Cox: Three hundreds not enough to keep Buttler out

metadata.summary: Jordan Cox insists Jos Buttler has earned the right to come back into England's ODI side, even if he was to score three hundreds while the country's "best ever" white-ball player recovers from injury.
metadata.content: Jordan Cox: Three hundreds not enough to keep Jos Buttler out - 'England's best ever' | Cricket News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Jordan Cox: Three hundreds not enough to keep Jos Buttler out - 'England's best ever' England's Jordan Cox ahead of series-deciding third ODI vs Australia quips scoring three hundreds would not be enough to keep Jos Buttler out of the side when latter returns, hailing him 'England's best ever' Tuesday 17 November 2026 11:42, UK Image: England's Jordan Cox hopes to play a pivotal role in the ODI series decider against Australia in Hobart on Wednesday Jordan Cox insists Jos Buttler has earned the right to come back into England's ODI side, even if he was to score three hundreds while the country's "best ever" white-ball player recovers from injury. Cox will continue to bat and keep wicket in the ODI series decider against Australia at Hobart's Bellerive Oval on Wednesday, having scored a lively 67 in England's series-levelling win in Adelaide last time out. He owes his place in the XI to Buttler's torn hamstring and is pragmatic when it comes to his prospects of keeping the shirt for next year's World Cup campaign. Asked about his chances of winning that particular selection battle, he said: "I don't think so, no. I think what Jos has done for English cricket in general [is too much].
